days.title: Northern Volcanic Slopes and Whaling History
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Brekkukambur
stops.detail: In the interior of the fjord there was an active central volcano in the Tertiary, which is why hot springs and rhyolite rock can be found on the slopes of the north side of the fjord on Mount Brekkukambur above the whaling station.

stops.name: Walfangstation
stops.detail: In the interior of Hvalfjörður, on its northern side, Iceland's most important whaling station was operated until the 1980s.

stops.name: Grundartangi
stops.detail: At Grundartangi there is an aluminum plant belonging to the company Norðurál as well as a ferrosilicon plant.

stops.name: Hvalfjarðargöng
stops.detail: Nowadays, the journey is shortened by the Hvalfjarðargöng tunnel under the fjord.

days.title: Fjord Interior and Ancient Trading Posts
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Botnsvogur
stops.detail: Two bays in particular branch off from it in the interior of the fjord: Botnsvogur and Brynjudalsvogur.

stops.name: Maríuhöfn
stops.detail: In the 14th century, for example, what was probably Iceland's most important trading post, Maríuhöfn, was located on the south shore of the fjord near Kjós.

stops.name: Hvalfjarðareyri
stops.detail: Another trading post was located in the interior of the fjord at the mouth of the river Laxá í Kjós: Hvalfjarðareyri.

days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Múlafell
stops.detail: In this regard, Múlafell and Þyrill are the remains of an extinct shield volcano.

stops.name: Saurbær à Hvalfjarðarströnd
stops.detail: In the parish of Saurbær à Hvalfjarðarströnd, the psalm poet and pastor Hallgrímur Pétursson lived and died in the 17th century.

stops.name: Glymur
stops.detail: The Glymur waterfall (meaning 'reverberation') traces its name back to the same event.
